# A win32 program in C runs its tests in the C test agent, cross-compiled
# with MinGW's compiler and run under Wine in a prefix of the cache's, whose
# windows the null driver draws; the agent connects back to the driver over
# TCP, since Wine hands a Windows program none of the host's pipes
# (codegen/platform/win32/launcher.go). A build rooted at the component a
# test takes renders it as the package body would, and a test's trigger is
# the platform's #[gen.fires] for the event the program's handler is
# connected to: a button's press, a check box's state, an edit's text as it
# is typed and as Enter commits it. A node a branch renders is held while it
# is rendered and null once taken away, and a test taking no component
# builds the program's window.

sngl test --platform=win32 --language=c app.sngl
stdout 'ok +3 tests, 0 failures'

# The same agent built for 32-bit Windows.

sngl test --platform=win32 --language=c --opt arch=386 app.sngl
stdout 'ok +3 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import test "sngl:test"

output {
    c {
        win32
    }
}

component main ui.node {
    var n = 0
    var name = ""
    var typed = ""
    var on = false
    ui.vbox {
        ui.text(value="Count {n}")
        ui.button #inc(text="More", @click { n += 1 })
        ui.button #dec(text="Less", @click { n -= 1 })
        ui.input #who(value=name, @input(v) { typed = v }, @change(v) { name = v })
        ui.checkbox #flag(checked=on, @change(v) { on = v })
        if n > 1 {
            ui.text #big(value="Big")
        }
    }
}

ui.window(title="Counter") {
    main()
}

func testPressesReachTheirHandlers(t test.Test, c main) {
    c.inc.click()
    t.assert(c.n == 1)
    t.assert(c.big == null)
    c.inc.click()
    t.assert(c.big != null)
    c.dec.click()
    t.assert(c.n == 1)
    t.assert(c.big == null)
}

func testValuesReachTheirHandlers(t test.Test, c main) {
    c.who.input("an")
    t.assert(c.typed == "an")
    t.assert(c.name == "")
    c.who.change("ann")
    t.assert(c.name == "ann")
    c.flag.change(true)
    t.assert(c.on)
    c.flag.change(false)
    t.assert(!c.on)
}

func testTheWindowBuilds(t test.Test) {
    t.assert(true)
}
